answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation grow slowly and decay when idle, like a grove that takes seasons to mature. New identities start with a tiny transaction quota, regardless of how many are created, and only earn higher limits through verified completed work over time. Cheap mass-created accounts therefore stay stuck at the bottom, while a basalt-solid history of useful service is expensive to fake: an attacker would need to fund real work for every fake identity, and an orchard of fresh Sybils yields no fruit until each one has genuinely served others.
